# link-fragments

- ID: `MD051`
- Category: Links and images
- Default: on, severity warning
- Fixable: no
- Tags: `links`

Links to a \#fragment point at a heading or anchor in the same file, or at
\#top.

## Why

A heading's anchor changes when the heading is renamed or removed, and a link to
the old anchor goes nowhere. In HTML, an element's id attribute, or the name
attribute of an a element, makes an anchor. Links to GitHub line numbers, such
as \#L20, pass too.

## Options

Set them under `rules.link-fragments.options`.

- `ignore_case` (`boolean`, default `false`): Match fragments to anchors in any
  case.
- `ignored_pattern` (`string`, default `""`): Regular expression for fragments
  that are not checked. Empty checks every fragment.

## Fix

There is no automatic fix. Only the author knows the intended target.

## Configure

```yaml
rules:
  link-fragments:
    options:
      ignore_case: false
```

Under `rules`, `link-fragments: false` turns the rule off and
`link-fragments: error` reports its findings as errors. The flag
`--disable link-fragments` turns it off for one run.

## Silence one line

```markdown
<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line link-fragments -->
```
